\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{FABL.Chapter09.VarianceSensitiveLargeCoefficient}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Variance-based Friedgut error]
\lean{FABL.varianceFriedgutError}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p268-b003}
\label{FABL.varianceFriedgutError}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.variance}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$. The variance-based
Friedgut error of $f$ is $\operatorname{Var}(f)/8$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Variance-based Friedgut degree]
\lean{FABL.varianceFriedgutDegree}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p268-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p269-b004
}
\label{FABL.varianceFriedgutDegree}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.friedgutDegree, FABL.varianceFriedgutError}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$. Its variance-based
Friedgut degree is the Friedgut degree of $f$ at error tolerance
$\operatorname{Var}(f)/8$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Variance-based Friedgut coordinates]
\lean{FABL.varianceFriedgutCoordinates}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p268-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p269-b004
}
\label{FABL.varianceFriedgutCoordinates}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.friedgutCoordinates, FABL.varianceFriedgutError}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$. Its variance-based
Friedgut coordinates are the coordinates selected by the Friedgut coordinate
construction for $f$ at error tolerance $\operatorname{Var}(f)/8$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Formula for the variance-based Friedgut degree]
\lean{FABL.varianceFriedgutDegree_eq}
\label{FABL.varianceFriedgutDegree_eq}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.friedgutDegree, FABL.totalInfluence, FABL.variance, FABL.varianceFriedgutDegree, FABL.varianceFriedgutError}
\difficulty{3}
Let $f$ be a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube, and suppose its variance
is positive. Its Friedgut degree at error equal to one eighth of its variance is the
ceiling of eight times its total influence divided by its variance.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Bound on the number of influential coordinates]
\lean{FABL.card_varianceFriedgutCoordinates_le}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p268-b003}
\label{FABL.card_varianceFriedgutCoordinates_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.card_friedgutCoordinates_le, FABL.totalInfluence, FABL.variance, FABL.varianceFriedgutCoordinates, FABL.varianceFriedgutDegree, FABL.varianceFriedgutError, FABL.variance_le_totalInfluence}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $f$ be a function from the $n$-dimensional Boolean
cube to $\{-1,1\}$. If the variance of the associated real-valued function is positive,
then the number of variance-Friedgut coordinates of $f$ is at most $64
I(f)^3\,9^d/\operatorname{Var}(f)^2$, where $I(f)$ is its total influence and $d$ is its
variance-Friedgut degree.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Variance-based large-coefficient family]
\lean{FABL.varianceLargeCoeffFamily}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p270-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p270-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p276-b007
}
\label{FABL.varianceLargeCoeffFamily}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.lowDegreeSubsets, FABL.varianceFriedgutCoordinates, FABL.varianceFriedgutDegree}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$. Form the family of
low-degree subsets on the variance-based Friedgut coordinates of $f$, using its
variance-based Friedgut degree as the degree bound, and remove the empty subset.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Characterization of the large coefficient family]
\lean{FABL.mem_varianceLargeCoeffFamily}
\label{FABL.mem_varianceLargeCoeffFamily}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.mem_lowDegreeSubsets, FABL.varianceFriedgutCoordinates, FABL.varianceFriedgutDegree, FABL.varianceLargeCoeffFamily}
\difficulty{3}
For a Boolean function $f$ on the $n$-dimensional sign cube and a subset $S$ of its
coordinates, $S$ belongs to the family of large-coefficient sets associated to $f$ if
and only if $S$ is contained in the selected Friedgut coordinates of $f$, its
cardinality is at most the variance-based Friedgut degree of $f$, and $S$ is nonempty.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fourier weight on the selected family]
\lean{FABL.three_variance_div_four_le_sum_varianceLargeCoeffFamily}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p270-b002}
\label{FABL.three_variance_div_four_le_sum_varianceLargeCoeffFamily}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.IsFourierSpectrumConcentratedOn, FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.fourierWeightOutside, FABL.friedgutCoordinates, FABL.friedgutDegree, FABL.friedgut_spectrum_concentrated, FABL.lowDegreeSubsets, FABL.mean_eq_fourierCoeff_empty, FABL.sum_fourierWeight_mem_add_outside_eq_one, FABL.totalInfluence, FABL.variance, FABL.varianceFriedgutCoordinates, FABL.varianceFriedgutDegree, FABL.varianceFriedgutError, FABL.varianceLargeCoeffFamily, FABL.variance_eq_four_mul_probabilities, FABL.variance_le_totalInfluence}
\difficulty{5}
Let $f$ be a Boolean function on the sign cube of dimension $n$ with positive variance.
Let $\mathcal F$ consist of all nonempty coordinate sets contained in the variance-based
Friedgut coordinate set whose size is at most the variance-based Friedgut degree. Then
$3\operatorname{Var}(f)/4$ is at most the sum of the squared Fourier coefficients of $f$
over $S\in\mathcal F$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[A large Fourier coefficient for a nonconstant Boolean function]
\lean{FABL.exists_varianceSensitive_large_fourierCoeff}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p276-b007}
\label{FABL.exists_varianceSensitive_large_fourierCoeff}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.IsNonconstantProductFunction, FABL.PMFHasFullSupport, FABL.Sign, FABL.card_lowDegreeSubsets_le, FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.mem_varianceLargeCoeffFamily, FABL.productVariance, FABL.productVariance_pos_of_nonconstant, FABL.productVariance_uniformSign, FABL.signValue_injective, FABL.three_variance_div_four_le_sum_varianceLargeCoeffFamily, FABL.uniformPMF, FABL.variance, FABL.varianceFriedgutCoordinates, FABL.varianceFriedgutDegree, FABL.varianceLargeCoeffFamily}
\difficulty{6}
Let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be nonconstant. Write $V$ for its variance under the
uniform measure, $I$ for its total influence, $D=\lceil 8I/V\rceil$, and $\tau=(V/8)^2
I^{-2}9^{-D}$. Let $J$ be the set of coordinates whose Boolean influence is at least
$\tau$. Then some nonempty set $S\subseteq[n]$ with $|S|\le D$ satisfies $\widehat
f(S)^2\ge V/[2(D+1)(|J|+1)^D]$.
\end{theorem}
